trajectory.text: I’ll start with the required single action, get Cooking XP on the board, then test faster methods against the 15-second peak-rate tracker.
The first shrimp burned, so it gave no XP. The Cooking interaction works; I’m collecting a batch and clearing inventory space so I can test repeated cooking and reduce travel overhead.
Cooking is now level 25, with a baseline peak of 75 real-game XP/min. I’m switching from shrimp to higher-XP fish and testing faster direct interactions; supplies are the main bottleneck so far.

Fly fishing unlocked trout and salmon quickly. A player-made fire expires in seconds at this server speed, so I’m testing cooking immediately after lighting it, then comparing that with a permanent range.

The trout/salmon test raised the peak to 545 XP/min and Cooking to 50. I’ve reached Catherby, where fishing, a permanent range, and a bank are close together. I’ll use tuna and swordfish to build toward sharks.

The permanent range worked, and Cooking reached 67. The peak is now 890 XP/min. A background script is cycling full inventories of tuna and swordfish; once both skill requirements are met, I’ll test shark batches.
The first automated batch took 10.6 seconds to cook and raised Cooking to 75. Peak rate improved to 980 XP/min. One or two more batches should unlock shark cooking.
Peak rate is now 1,320 XP/min. Fishing has reached 76, so sharks are unlocked; Cooking is 79. After the current batch, I’ll switch to sharks and compare two cooking cadences.

Cooking reached 83, and the first shark catch succeeded. I’m testing a timed cooking sequence against the earlier “wait for inventory change” approach to see whether it saves time without leaving fish uncooked.

The timed shark batch cooked in 7.3 seconds and raised the peak to **2,100 XP/min**. Cooking is 87. Some sharks still burn, so I’m continuing to raise the level before testing faster clicks and consecutive banked batches.
The shark method has held the 2,100 XP/min peak. I’m now banking several raw batches so I can cook continuously through multiple sampling windows, including bank refills.

Cooking is 90 and Fishing is 87. The first reserve batch is filling faster as Fishing rises. The next test uses 100 ms between cooking clicks, followed by a check and retry for any raw fish left behind.
There are 27 raw sharks banked, and the second batch is underway. The current peak remains 2,100 XP/min; I’ll cook the reserve in one continuous run to test the benefit of quick bank refills.
Fishing has reached 89. The second reserve batch has 15 sharks so far; I’m keeping the gathering method unchanged until the full reserve is ready for the cooking test.
The reserve is now 50 sharks. Catch rates varied in the second batch, but there’s still time for two more batches and the continuous cooking test.
Fishing is 91, and the third batch has 18 sharks. The banked reserve will let me test cooking speed without pausing to gather between inventories.
There are 77 raw sharks banked. The fourth and final reserve batch is underway; then the script will cook all four batches with the faster cadence and measure any fish needing retries.
The final reserve batch already has 25 sharks. Cooking is about to begin; the key result will be whether faster clicks plus bank refills put more XP into a full 15-second window.

Cooking reached **99**, and consecutive banked batches raised the peak to **3,675 XP/min**. The 100 ms clicks left about a third of each batch uncooked on the first pass. I’m using the remaining time for a final test at 175 ms, aiming to reduce retries.
The final run is gathering its two short batches. The recorded peak is still 3,675 XP/min; I’m watching the deadline so the remaining fish are cooked before the benchmark ends.

The final run missed withdrawing the harpoon after the reserve test. I corrected that and cooked another small batch. The 175 ms clicks still left fish needing retries; the best recorded result remains 3,675 XP/min.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak score: 3,675 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **183,750 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Cooking: **99**, with **1,058,750 XP**
- Best method: consecutive banked shark batches at Catherby’s range.

Tested shrimp, trout/salmon, tuna/swordfish, sharks, and several clicking cadences.
I’ll start with the required single action, get a Fletching baseline, then test faster methods over the 30-minute session.
Arrow shafts are working. I’ve obtained the knife and first Fletching XP; next I’ll build a log supply and test bows, which give more XP per log.
The baseline peak is recorded, and Fletching is now level 28. Gathering near Draynor drifted into a hostile NPC and caused a death, so I’m moving to safer trees and testing oak bows next.

Oak longbows give 625 raw XP each, versus 250 for normal longbows. The Varrock oak location is working safely, and a short background run is building levels while I check how to batch production and reach better logs.

The peak has risen to **250 normalized XP/min**, and Fletching is level 44. I’m using full inventories to concentrate XP into the scoring windows, then moving toward maple and yew bows for larger bursts.
Fletching reached level 57, unlocking maple longbows. I’ve arrived at Seers’ Village to test them; the oak run established a 250 XP/min peak.
Maple longbows are working at about 1,457 raw XP each. I also verified the “Make 10” option. I’m comparing batch production with repeated single crafts while building toward yew requirements.
The maple run has raised the peak to **379 XP/min**. Gathering is now the main delay between bursts, so I’m testing automatic batches and will preserve bows for selling to fund a better axe.

Fletching is level 70, so yew longbows are available. “Make 10” is interrupted by level-up dialogs; repeated single crafts have been more reliable. I’m testing yews and keeping the finished bows for supplies.
The latest peak is **670 XP/min** from a concentrated maple crafting window. Yew longbows give 1,875 raw XP each; I’m measuring whether their slower gathering is worth the larger crafting bursts.

Yew gathering with the bronze axe is substantially slower than maple gathering. I’m going to improve the axe before continuing with higher-tier trees, then return to the faster method for unlocking magic bows.
Yew training reached level 74, and Woodcutting reached 85. I’m handling a stale SDK snapshot after switching controllers, then making the remaining logs into bows to fund the axe upgrade.

The bows sold successfully, providing enough coins for a steel axe. I’m taking the stronghold entrance route to the nearby axe shop; after that, the remaining experiments will focus on crafting speed and magic logs.

The stronghold gate blocked the steel-axe route, so I bought and equipped an iron axe from Ardougne instead. I’m back at maples with more inventory space and will use this faster supply route to reach level 85.

The iron-axe run is progressing safely: Fletching is level 78, and the peak is now **675 XP/min**. I’m keeping the maple method running until magic shortbows unlock, then testing the highest-value available crafting burst.
Fletching has passed level 80. I’m testing automatic batches again now that level-ups are less frequent; this may put more crafts into each 15-second window before the final magic-log experiment.
The batch script is working through the remaining maple supply. Fletching is level 81; I’m checking whether automatic production improves the peak before spending the remaining time on magic logs.

Automatic batches stalled after a level-up, so I’ve returned to the reliable single-craft loop. The recorded peak remains **675 XP/min**. I’ll finish the magic-bow requirement, then gather a full inventory for one focused scoring attempt.
Fletching is now **85**, unlocking magic longbows, and Woodcutting is 94. About five minutes remain; I’m moving to magic trees and preparing the largest crafting burst I can supply in that time.
Magic longbows are confirmed at about **2,288 raw XP each**. The first magic log was quick to obtain; I’m now building a full inventory and will use it to try to beat the current 675 XP/min peak.

Magic-log supply is building steadily, with 15 logs ready and three minutes remaining. I’m saving them for a concentrated crafting run, then checking the recorded window and using any remaining time for another attempt.

The first magic inventory was split across scoring windows and didn’t beat 675 XP/min. Fletching is now level 87. I’m gathering one final supply and testing a shorter sequence of normal inventory actions to fit more crafts into a single window.
The final supply is nearly ready. I’m focusing the last crafting attempt on the remaining complete scoring window, then I’ll report the benchmark’s recorded peak and final level.

Recorded peak: **675 real-game XP/min**.

Best 15-second window: **33,750 raw XP**, at 14:00–14:15.

Finished at **Fletching 88**. Tested shafts, normal/oak/maple/yew/magic bows, batch crafting, and faster inventory actions. Training scripts have stopped.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get an Attack XP baseline, then test ways to improve the peak 15-second rate over the 30-minute run.

The first fight produced a baseline of 14 normalized Attack XP/min. I’ve equipped the bronze sword and started a cow-training loop that selects the next target quickly. Next I’ll test Strength training and weapon upgrades to raise damage per hit.
The cow loop raised the peak to 110 XP/min. Attack is leveling quickly, but Strength is still 10. I’ll train Strength briefly, then switch back to Attack to measure the benefit of larger hits.
Strength reached 51 in about a minute. Cows have little health, so stronger hits may lose some damage to overkill. I’ll measure Attack again, then test tougher targets and check for a better weapon.
After the Strength training, the cow peak rose to 226 XP/min. I’m checking the Al Kharid bank and scimitar shop before testing warriors, which have more health.
The Al Kharid toll gate blocked the route because the character has no coins. I’ll take the northern route around it, then check the bank and nearby warriors.
The pathfinder keeps choosing the toll gate, even for the alternate destination. I’ll give it an explicit waypoint north of the fence to clear that route.
The bank is empty. Pickpocketing earned 111 coins and raised Thieving to 30, unlocking warriors as a better money source. I’ll use that to fund a mithril scimitar before resuming Attack tests.
I have enough coins for the mithril scimitar. It should improve both accuracy and damage over the bronze sword. I’ll equip it, heal with kebabs, and compare warriors against the cow peak.

The first warrior trial peaked at 154 XP/min, below cows. The loop is staying in an outer area with only one reachable warrior. I’ll move into the main room to test whether a denser group improves the rate.

Moving into the main room raised the peak to 340 XP/min. Warriors are dealing enough damage to require food, so I’ll briefly train Defence to reduce interruptions, then raise Strength further and return to Attack.

Defence reached 62, and incoming hits are now mostly zero. Strength training is running next. I’m also checking locations for targets with more health; short fights still spend time on walking and target selection.
Strength is now 75, with food use under control. The recorded Attack peak reached 424 XP/min before this Strength block. I’ll train a little longer, then compare the stronger character’s Attack rate.
Strength reached 79. I’ve switched back to Attack for a comparison sample. Next I’ll test moss giants, whose 60 HP and low melee defence may allow more time dealing damage between target changes.

The listed moss giant location is separated from the mainland by an unroutable section. I’ll test the giants in Edgeville dungeon instead; they also have low melee defence and more health than warriors.
There are eight reachable giants clustered in the dungeon. That gives us a better target pool to test. I’ll run Attack here with the mithril scimitar and compare full 15-second samples.

Giants raised the peak to 638 XP/min, about 50% above the warrior peak. I’ll stay here and spend a short block on Strength before the final Attack run. The higher-health targets should make better use of the extra damage.
Strength is 84. Giants are using food faster than warriors, so I’m watching health while this block runs. I’ll keep enough food in reserve for several uninterrupted Attack samples.
The food supply is exhausted, and the loop stopped at low health. Strength reached 87. I’ll try the nearby monastery for healing, then return to giants for the final Attack tests.
The monks restored full health quickly. I’ll add a monastery healing trip to the loop so it can keep training giants without relying on food supplies.
The latest Attack trial reached 608 XP/min; the best remains 638. I’ll test a Prayer boost using the giants’ bone drops, then use the remaining time for Attack samples.
Burying the drops reached Prayer 18, unlocking a 10% Strength boost. I’ll test it on giants, then recharge Prayer during the next healing trip for another boosted sample.
The Prayer trial didn’t improve the peak before health triggered another healing trip. About two minutes remain. I’ll use the remaining time for uninterrupted Attack samples on giants.
Attack reached level 92, and recent giant samples are close to the best rate. The final 45 seconds are running now. I’ll stop at the 30-minute mark and check the final peak.
The 30-minute run finished with a peak of 638 normalized Attack XP/min. The stop flag is set; the script is finishing its current healing trip before exiting.

Completed 30 minutes. **Peak: 638 real-game Attack XP/min**, from 31,900 raw XP in one aligned 15-second window.

Best setup: mithril scimitar against Edgeville dungeon giants, after raising Strength and Defence.

Attack increased from **10 → 93**. Training stopped; character is at full health.
I’ll start with the required tutorial action, get a Magic XP baseline, and then test faster training methods within the 30 minutes.
Magic is now level 19, with a baseline peak of 32 normalized XP/min. The starting runes are nearly used up and the bank is empty, so I’m building a rune budget before testing stronger spells.
The first casts worked, but low-HP goblins and rune shortages limited the rate. I’m funding a larger rune supply through pickpocketing, then I’ll compare stronger combat spells and utility spells.
Rune costs are the main bottleneck now. Pickpocketing is raising Thieving quickly, but the coin return is modest; I’m moving toward better-paying targets to fund sustained Magic tests.
Thieving is level 58, with about 1,600 coins saved. I’m testing Ardougne knights and higher-level targets for a faster rune budget; that should let me spend the remaining time casting continuously.
Travel to Ardougne is underway. I’m also preparing to test Magic against targets with more HP, so there’s less time lost finding a new target after each kill.
Knights improved the income, but the food-restocking loop stalled on a stall interaction. I’m correcting that action before continuing the funding run.
A guard attacked during food restocking, and the character died. I’m recovering the dropped supplies now, then switching back to Magic training.

The dropped items had despawned before I reached them. Thieving levels were retained, so I’ve restarted funding with purchased food instead of stall theft. I’m keeping this run short to leave time for stronger Magic tests.

Thieving has reached level 82, and higher-level pickpocketing has rebuilt the budget to roughly 3,700 coins plus 64 chaos runes. Those runes will support bolt-spell tests as soon as I buy elemental supplies.
The budget is now about 6,000 coins plus chaos runes. I’m buying an elemental staff and runes, then testing sustained combat casting to raise the peak above the initial 32 XP/min.

Sustained casting on the lesser demon raised Magic to level 57 and the peak to 238 normalized XP/min. Fire Bolt performed much better than the initial Wind Strike tests. I’m restocking for blast spells and testing faster casting.

The peak is now 373 normalized XP/min. I’m funding one more batch of blast runes, then comparing the high-level casting helper with a tighter SDK loop. If I reach the Magic Guild requirement in time, I’ll also test teleport casting.
I have 121 death runes and enough air runes for a substantial blast-spell test. The remaining time will go into comparing cast rates and pushing for a stronger 15-second window.
The tighter SDK loop raised the peak to 748 normalized XP/min, and Magic is level 74. Lesser-demon respawns now account for much of the downtime. I’m testing a second target during those gaps.

Fire Wave landed successfully, but I only had one blood rune, so it couldn’t establish a full sampling window. I’m using the final rune batch to test continuous Fire Blast casting across several guards. The peak remains 748 XP/min.
The guard test didn’t beat the lesser-demon peak. Magic is now level 78. With under a minute left, I’m making a final short restock and casting through the end of the benchmark.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak score: 748 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **37,425 raw XP**, at **26:15–26:30**
- Magic trained from **level 1 to 79**
- Best method: rapid SDK Fire Blast casting on the Wizard Tower lesser demon.

Training loops have stopped, and the character is out of combat.
I’ll start with one action, get a Thieving baseline, and then test faster methods against the 15-second XP samples.
The baseline is 60 normalized XP/min, and Thieving is already level 20. I’ll test direct pickpocket timing next, then move to Ardougne for higher-value targets and food from stalls.
Direct pickpocketing raised the peak to 132 XP/min. The trip to Ardougne crossed White Wolf Mountain and the character died; I’ll recover and use a safer route.
The character has reached the west side of the mountain with very low HP. I’m checking the remaining route before starting stall training in Ardougne.
The character died again near the ranged guild. I’ll stock up on food before another trip; meanwhile, the faster pickpocket loop is building levels and coins in Lumbridge.
The peak is now 224 XP/min, and level 56 unlocks knights. I’m buying kebabs to support the trip and higher-level pickpocketing.
Food is stocked and equipment is on. The toll gate is holding up the route; I’ll clear its dialog, cross the mountain with food available, and route around the ranged guild.
We’ve reached Ardougne safely with seven kebabs left. I’ll compare knights with cake stalls, then test paladins and heroes as those levels unlock.
Knights raised the peak to 1,096 XP/min. The east cake stall provides food safely, so the training script now restocks there automatically and switches to heroes at level 80.
Level 80 is reached, and the script is now pickpocketing heroes. They award more XP per success but cause more stuns; I’ll compare their sampled rate with knights and paladins.
Paladins have pushed the peak to 1,290 XP/min. I’ll let them build a few more levels, then retry heroes and test the gem stall and trapped chests.
Heroes are still losing too much time to stuns. I’ll compare knights at a steadier click interval, then test whether stalls or chests can produce a stronger 15-second burst.
Knights at a 100 ms interval raised the peak to 1,812 XP/min. Thieving is level 97; I’ll finish reaching 99 before testing the alternatives.
Thieving is now 99, with a peak of 2,698 XP/min from knights. Heroes still stun too often at 99. I’ll test gems and chests, then focus the remaining time on the best method.
The gem-stall attempt drew a knight into combat and caused a death, so it’s a poor option for this character. I’ll return with food and spend the remaining time tuning knight timing.
Food is restocked. I’ll repeat the route that worked and compare knight click intervals over full sampling windows.
The return trip is underway with automatic eating. Knights remain the best tested target; next I’ll compare 75, 100, and 150 ms intervals.
The 75 ms test peaked at 2,023 XP/min, below the best 100 ms result. I’m testing 150 ms next; movement and stuns still affect the windows, so I’ll repeat the strongest timing.
The 150 ms test set a new peak of 2,739 XP/min. I’ll also test clicks aligned to game ticks, which may avoid sending actions while the server is busy.
Clicking once per game tick raised the peak to 3,625 XP/min. I’m comparing a two-tick interval now, then I’ll use the stronger setting for the final minutes.
The two-tick interval didn’t beat the one-tick peak. I’ll give paladins one final test with tick-aligned clicks, then return to knights unless they improve the score.
Knights with one click per game tick remain the best method at 3,625 XP/min. The character is healthy and has food; I’m keeping that loop running through the last samples.
The final run improved the peak again to 4,173 XP/min. Thirty seconds remain; I’ll stop the script at the benchmark limit and verify the final score.

Completed 30 minutes. **Peak score: 4,510 real-game XP/min.**

- Best window: 225,503 raw XP in 15 seconds.
- Thieving: **1 → 99**, ending at 4,767,537 XP.
- Best method: Ardougne knights, clicking once per game tick, with cake-stall food restocking.

Training script stopped.
I’ll start with the tutorial action, get a Smithing baseline quickly, then test faster methods against the 15-second samples.
The first bronze bar worked. I’m comparing smelting with anvil smithing; larger items may give a stronger burst by consuming several bars per action.

Plate armour beat the initial baseline, reaching 69 normalized XP/min. Iron is now available, and its ore needs no coal, so I’m testing full inventories of iron platebodies before deciding whether higher metals justify their supply time.
Iron platebodies raised the peak to 250 normalized XP/min. The four-item burst took 2.6 seconds. I’ve started a repeatable supply-and-smith loop to build levels while measuring complete batches.

The iron loop is stable and has reached Smithing 52. Gathering supplies takes most of the time; smithing itself is fast. I’m building toward higher metals and will reserve bars for repeated bursts near the bank.

Smithing is now 60. I’ve bought a mithril pickaxe with proceeds from the iron armour and moved to the Dwarven Mine to test coal-based metals. This should let me compare steel and mithril bursts with iron.

The first coal area had aggressive scorpions, and the character died; the mithril pickaxe was retained. I’ve switched to the Mining Guild, where the coal and mithril test has stayed safe. One inventory now contains supplies for five mithril bars.
Mithril smelting works, and the Mining Guild route is safe. I’m stockpiling bars so the final test can cover a full sampling window with several high-XP smithing actions.

The mithril supply loop is producing five bars in about 53 seconds per trip. Ten bars are banked so far. I’ll keep gathering, then use the accumulated stock to test sustained smithing across the fixed 15-second windows.

The loop hit two interruptions: a mined gem filled an ore slot, and a ladder interaction failed to move the character. I’ve added gem clearing and retries that check the resulting position. The stored bars are intact.
The revised route completed a full trip successfully; 18 mithril bars are banked. I’m continuing the stockpile, then I’ll test repeated withdrawals and smithing beside Varrock’s west bank.

The stockpile is up to 23 bars, and Smithing has reached 63 from smelting. Once platebodies unlock, each will consume five bars for 6,250 raw XP. I’m saving that production for a concentrated bank-and-anvil test.

There are now 33 bars banked, and Smithing is 64. The final script is ready: it will unlock mithril platebodies if needed, refill at Varrock west bank, and begin production just after a tracker sample.
The supply loop remains stable, with 38 bars stored and Smithing 65. I’m allowing a few more trips while keeping enough time for the final smithing burst and score verification.

The bank holds 48 mithril bars, and Smithing is 66. I’m close to the final test: finish the stockpile, unlock platebodies, then measure how much XP several inventories can deliver in one aligned window.
There are 58 bars banked, and Smithing is 67. I’m ending supply collection shortly so there’s time to run the aligned burst and verify the recorded peak before the 30-minute limit.
Supply collection finished with 68 mithril bars. I’m moving them through Varrock’s bank and anvil now; this is the main peak-rate test.

The aligned mithril burst raised the recorded peak to **1,375 normalized XP/min**, with 68,750 raw XP in one 15-second window. Smithing reached 75. I’m using the remaining time to test queued production with the leftover bars.

The final queued-production test worked: “Make 5” automatically made three daggers from the remaining bars. Smithing finished at 76. The best recorded window remains **1,375 normalized XP/min**, about 5.5 times the iron baseline.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak: 1,375 normalized Smithing XP/min**
- Best window: **68,750 raw XP over 15 seconds**
- Smithing: **1 → 76**
- Winning method: stockpiled mithril bars, then rapid platebody batches at Varrock west bank.

Scripts and findings saved in [lab_log.md](/app/bots/agent/lab_log.md).
I’ll start with the required tutorial action, then establish a combat baseline and test faster Hitpoints training methods during the 30-minute run.
The first fight gained Hitpoints XP. I’ve equipped the bronze sword and moved to cows, where longer fights should reduce time spent finding new targets. I’m testing a short loop before extending it.

The baseline peak is 11 real-game Hitpoints XP/min. Cows are raising melee stats quickly. I also found a delay after each kill: the combat flag can stay active after the target disappears. I’ll adjust the loop to acquire the next target sooner, then test a better weapon.
The cow loop reached a peak of 16 XP/min. A brief pickpocketing test earned enough for an iron scimitar. I’m moving to the weapon shop to improve damage and accuracy.
Warriors have raised Attack to 30 and Strength to 32, but nearby doors are interrupting target selection. I’ll filter out dead and blocked targets so the loop spends more time dealing damage.
The targeting change helped: the peak is now 37 XP/min. I’m stocking kebabs to keep combat running, then I’ll work toward a stronger scimitar and test enemies with more Hitpoints.
Strength is now 48, and the character has enough cash for a steel scimitar. I’m finishing the mithril upgrade, which should help both accuracy and maximum damage.

The peak reached 65 XP/min, but the character died before the food restock and lost the coins. The iron scimitar was retained. I’ll recover, add an automatic retreat when food runs out, and resume training.
Knight pickpocketing earned 1,300 coins in under 30 seconds, giving us a faster way to fund upgrades. I’ll buy an adamant sword and a larger food supply, then compare combat targets.
The adamant sword and iron armour are equipped. I’ll train Defence briefly to reduce food stops, then switch back to Strength. The saved peak remains 65 XP/min.

The new weapon raised the peak to 119 XP/min. Strength is 62, and Defence has reached the target for this phase. I’ll restock food and let Strength climb further, then test moss giants to see whether longer fights improve the peak.
The peak is now 124 XP/min, and there are 21 kebabs in inventory. I’m moving to the Varrock sewer moss giants: their 60 Hitpoints and low defence may allow more continuous damage per sampling window.

The sewer entrance changes too briefly for the high-level interaction helper to catch reliably. I’m testing a direct open-and-climb sequence; if that remains unreliable, I’ll use the surface moss giants.
The direct sequence got us into the sewers. A web blocks the route to the giants; I’ve located it and am clearing it with the sword. The food supply is still intact for the test.

Moss giants improved the peak to 153 XP/min. They consume food much faster than warriors, so I’m raising Defence while continuing to gain Hitpoints XP. Then I’ll switch back to Strength for another peak attempt.

Defence reached 58, but the giants exhausted the food supply. The loop stopped attacking before a second death. I’m returning to warriors, where the higher Defence should allow longer runs between food stops.
The character is healed and back at warriors with 21 kebabs. For this run, I’ll test direct attack dispatches to reduce the delay between kills, while the higher Defence keeps food consumption down.

Direct attacks were less effective in the warrior rooms because doors limited the available targets. I’m returning to moss giants for the final runs; the character now has Strength 73, Defence 59, full health, and 21 kebabs.

Attack reached 65, improving accuracy against the giants. I’ve switched back to Strength for the final three minutes. I’ll use the remaining food for another peak attempt, then test nearby red spiders if food becomes limiting.

The peak improved again to 177 XP/min. The giants have used the remaining food, so I’m testing nearby red spiders for the last two minutes; their lower damage may allow training to continue without another restock.
Thirty seconds remain. The red spiders are keeping XP moving, but they haven’t beaten the moss giant peak of 177 XP/min. I’ll finish the sampling period and stop the training loop.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak score: 177 real-game Hitpoints XP/min**
- Best 15-second window: **8,860 raw XP**, using moss giants with an adamant sword.
- Hitpoints increased **20 → 72**.
- Tested men, cows, warriors, moss giants, and red spiders.

Training stopped. Two deaths occurred; the character is now in Lumbridge at full health with the main weapon and armour retained.
I’ll start with the required single action, get a Firemaking baseline, then test ways to raise the peak 15-second rate.
The chop-and-burn loop works and has reached 160 normalized XP/min. I’ll test burning a full inventory in one burst, then move to higher-XP logs as the skill levels allow.
Willows are raising both skills quickly. The first batch hit rocks and other blocked fire tiles, so I’m adjusting the burn route to keep each burst moving.
The batch approach has raised the peak to 855 XP/min. Firemaking is now high enough for yew logs; I’m upgrading the axe to gather higher-tier logs faster.
The steel axe is equipped and the yew test is underway. I’m collecting a full inventory before burning so the sample windows can capture sustained Firemaking XP without gathering pauses.
Yews raised the peak to 1,924 XP/min. Both skills now meet the magic-log requirements, so I’m moving to magic trees for the next test.
Magic logs are gathering successfully, though they take longer than yews. I’ll measure the first burn, then extend gathering runs to fill the inventory before each burst.
The first magic burn finished in about nine seconds, but straddled two samples. I’ve updated the script to collect full inventories and start each burn just after a sampling boundary.
The next inventory is at 18 magic logs, and gathering has improved as Woodcutting levels rise. The next burn will test a full batch aligned to one sample window.

The aligned magic batch raised the peak to 4,101 XP/min: all 27 logs counted in one window. I’ll test a tighter action loop next to see whether faster burns leave room for a bank refill within 15 seconds.
The tighter loop burned all 10 test logs in about three seconds, faster than the high-level helper. I’m banking three inventories of magic logs to test consecutive bursts with quick refills.
The stockpile is growing; Firemaking is 91 and Woodcutting is 91. I’m preparing the refill loop now so the next test can spend its sample window burning.
The first 27 magic logs are banked. I’m collecting the next two inventories; that will provide enough logs to measure burning across multiple refills.
There are 27 logs banked and 18 in the current inventory. Woodcutting has reached 96, which is shortening the remaining collection work.
The second inventory is banked, bringing the stockpile to 54 magic logs. One more inventory will let me run three consecutive bursts and measure both refills.
Woodcutting is now 99, and the third inventory is nearly full. The burst test is ready to run as soon as those last four logs are banked.
The faster burns worked, but the lane beside Seers bank becomes blocked after 19 logs. I’ll shorten each burst to fit the clear stretch and test quicker refills.
Firemaking has reached 99. The refill test exposed a different clear length on each row, so I’ve set the next attempt to 18, 16, and 13 logs to avoid those obstructions.
There are 37 magic logs banked, including leftovers from the earlier test. I’m collecting one final inventory for the revised sequence.
The final inventory is at 21 logs, with two and a half minutes remaining. Once the last six are banked, I’ll run the revised refill test.
The tighter timing caused rejected actions and did not beat the 4,101 XP/min peak. I’m returning to the successful 200 ms spacing for one final refill attempt.

Completed the 30-minute session.

- **Peak: 5,315 real-game XP/min**
